summary: Real mirrored reflections for a flat surface, rendered by a second camera into a low-res texture.
overview: A second camera renders the scene mirrored across this object's plane into a low-resolution RenderTexture, which the water shader samples in screen space. Real reflections rather than a cubemap approximation, at the cost of a second render of the scene.
useCases: Water that genuinely reflects the level.
Wet surfaces in a scene where a cubemap would look obviously wrong.

params.tuning: Exclude UI, the water itself, and anything that does not need reflecting. This is the main cost control — everything included is rendered a second time.
Reflections tolerate low resolution remarkably well. Halving this is usually invisible and much cheaper.
Still water can update every few frames with nobody noticing.
Pushes the clip plane slightly along the normal to stop artefacts right at the waterline. Too much and objects float visibly above their reflection.

gotchas.title: It renders the scene twice
gotchas.body: That is the whole technique. The mask and the resolution are the levers — there is no way to make it free.

gotchas.title: It only works for a FLAT plane
gotchas.body: Planar means planar. A rippling surface still reflects as if flat, which is why the normal perturbation carries the illusion.
